chunks.doc: Vehicle Registration — MPWT public service page
chunks.instrument: Prakas No. 262 PrK.SK.DChK dated 27 August 2019 on the formalities and procedures for registering vehicles, issuing vehicle registration plates and removing vehicles from the vehicle register
chunks.text: In Cambodia a vehicle must be registered according to the legal procedures before it may lawfully be driven on the road. A car may be registered by the owner directly through the ministry's automated vehicle registration system at https://vehicle.mpwt.gov.kh, where the owner selects the registration plate they prefer and enters the registration details themselves, without having to make any unofficial payments. The owner creates an account and enters their personal details and the vehicle details, and attaches images of the import tax receipt, the vehicle sale and purchase letter, the technical inspection certificate, and the Khmer national identity card or residence book or family book of the vehicle owner. The registration service fee is 125,000 riel, plus the price of the registration plate chosen.

chunks.instrument: Prakas No. 066 PrK.SK dated 1 February 2016 on the delegation of the motorcycle registration function to municipal, district and khan administrations through one-window service offices
chunks.text: A motorcycle or a three-wheeled motor vehicle may be registered at motorcycle dealers nationwide, at the Phnom Penh and provincial departments of public works and transport, or at the one-window service offices in every khan of Phnom Penh and in each province. The registration fee for a motorcycle or three-wheeled motor vehicle is 40,000 riel. The registration plate is received immediately at the place where registration is requested. The vehicle registration card for the motorcycle or three-wheeled motor vehicle is issued afterwards, once an officer has checked and approved it for printing.

chunks.instrument: Prakas No. 262 PrK.SK.DChK dated 27 August 2019 on the formalities and procedures for registering vehicles, issuing vehicle registration plates and removing vehicles from the vehicle register
chunks.text: The documents required for vehicle registration are an identity document, being the identity card, the family book or the residence book; the vehicle tax receipt; the sale and purchase letter; and the vehicle technical inspection certificate, which can be obtained within the automated registration system. Registration may be done by the owner through the automated system at https://vehicle.mpwt.gov.kh, or in person at the Ministry of Public Works and Transport, at Chip Mong Noro Mall, at the Phnom Penh and provincial departments of public works and transport, or at a vehicle dealer authorised to register with the ministry.

chunks.instrument: Prakas No. 089 PrK.SK.DChK dated 6 March 2018 on the delegation of the function of registering privately owned vehicles to capital, provincial, municipal and khan administrations
chunks.text: A vehicle is registered, and its plate issued, at the department of public works and transport of the province shown on the owner's identity card; an identity card issued in Phnom Penh means registration at the Phnom Penh department. chunks.doc: Vehicle Registration — reserving a plate number FAQ on the MPWT public service page
chunks.instrument: Prakas No. 262 PrK.SK.DChK dated 27 August 2019 on the formalities and procedures for registering vehicles, issuing vehicle registration plates and removing vehicles from the vehicle register
chunks.text: To order a reserved plate number, the applicant first creates an account in the system, searches for the number they want, then orders it and makes payment, after which the number becomes their property within the system. A number that has been ordered is valid for 30 days counted from the date payment was completed. After ordering, the applicant continues the registration by logging in to their account, completing the form as instructed and paying the registration service fee. Once the form is complete and the fee paid, the applicant waits for an email about the progress of the plate and the time to come and collect it. A plate number cannot be bought in another person's name.

chunks.instrument: Prakas No. 262 PrK.SK.DChK dated 27 August 2019 on the formalities and procedures for registering vehicles, issuing vehicle registration plates and removing vehicles from the vehicle register
chunks.text: An owner requesting retention of a number is not permitted to keep the plate and the registration card themselves. The owner must hand the plate and the vehicle registration card to the responsible officer for safekeeping, and the officer issues a number retention letter to the owner. Retention is valid for 90 days, within which the owner is required to register; otherwise the number is returned to the sale process, and money already paid is not refunded.

chunks.doc: Vehicle Registration — personalised special registration FAQ on the MPWT public service page
chunks.instrument: Inter-Ministerial Prakas No. 197 MEF.PrK.ATC dated 17 March 2025 on the sale and auction of personalised special registration numbers for vehicles
chunks.text: A personalised special number is a type of registration number whose plate carries the Khmer word for Cambodia at the top, a registration number of not more than 8 digits or Latin characters in the middle, and the Latin word CAMBODIA below a horizontal line at the bottom. The number may be used for life, and may be retained for registration against the holder's later vehicles. Prices run from 2 million riel to 1,000 million riel, which the ministry states as 500 to 250,000 US dollars. Prices are set, and numbers put to public auction, on the basis of: the fewer the digits the higher the price; words found in the English dictionary; the number 168; identical numbers or letters; numbers or letters running consecutively in ascending order; numbers or letters running consecutively in descending order; numbers or letters that are palindromic; consecutive odd or even numbers; and the individual characters. The ministry states that most 8-character numbers cost around 3 to 4 million riel, and that 1,000 million riel is the highest price set by the system, mostly for numbers with few characters.

chunks.doc: Vehicle Registration — ownership transfer documents FAQ on the MPWT public service page
chunks.instrument: Inter-Ministerial Prakas No. 264 PrK.SK.DChK dated 27 August 2020 on the formalities and procedures for transferring ownership of vehicles
chunks.text: Transfer of ownership covers two cases: transfer where the original owner is available, and transfer where the original owner cannot be found. Where the original owner is available, the documents include one application for transfer of ownership; two copies of the sale and purchase letter, completed and then thumbprinted in front of the officer by both the original owner and the final owner; and the identity cards of the original owner and of the final owner, photocopied and certified by the one-window office, with a patent certificate bearing the company stamp in the case of a company. Where the original owner cannot be found, the documents include one application for transfer of ownership; two guarantee contracts, completed and then certified by the police post where the final owner resides; the identity card of the original owner; the identity card of the final owner, photocopied and certified by the one-window office; and the sale and purchase letter. The source page lists further items for each case that are recorded in Khmer in this chunk. Transfer of ownership in Phnom Penh is done at the Ministry of Public Works and Transport or at Chip Mong Noro Mall, and in the provinces at the departments of public works and transport for the address of the buyer.

chunks.doc: Vehicle Registration — lost plate FAQ on the MPWT public service page
chunks.instrument: Inter-Ministerial Prakas No. 1460 MEF.PrK dated 31 December 2019 on the provision of public services by the Ministry of Public Works and Transport
chunks.text: Where a registration plate is lost, a duplicate plate may be requested. The documents required are a report of the loss of the plate; the vehicle registration card; the owner's identity card, together with the family book or residence book where the permanent address differs from the address on the identity card; an application for a duplicate registration plate, with the actual chassis and engine number rubbing attached; and the vehicle technical inspection certificate. The service fees are: small or light vehicle, single plate 38,000 riel and pair of plates 65,000 riel; small or light vehicle under personalised special registration, single plate 120,000 riel and pair 240,000 riel; large or heavy vehicle, single plate 52,000 riel and pair 70,000 riel; large or heavy vehicle under personalised special registration, single plate 150,000 riel and pair 300,000 riel; large-size plate, single 120,000 riel and pair 180,000 riel.

chunks.doc: Vehicle Registration — replacing a damaged or old plate FAQ on the MPWT public service page
chunks.instrument: Prakas No. 262 PrK.SK.DChK dated 27 August 2019 on the formalities and procedures for registering vehicles, issuing vehicle registration plates and removing vehicles from the vehicle register
chunks.text: A vehicle whose plate is old, bent or worn may request a new plate, but keeps the same series and the same number. The documents required are the old plate to be replaced; the vehicle registration card; the owner's identity card, together with the family book or residence book where the permanent address differs from the address on the identity card; and the vehicle technical inspection certificate. To exchange an old series plate for a new plate carrying a QR code, the documents required are an application for the exchange, the plate to be exchanged, the vehicle registration card, and the identity card or family book or residence book.

chunks.text: Once the registration details are complete, the applicant prints the invoice and pays at a Wing, SmartLuy or Ly Hour counter, or from their own Wing account. chunks.doc: Technical Inspection — MPWT public service page
chunks.instrument: Prakas No. 170 PrK.SK.DChK dated 12 June 2019 on the technical inspection of vehicles of all types
chunks.text: A vehicle must pass a technical inspection to prove its roadworthiness, and the technical inspection certificate is one of the documents required to register a vehicle. An appointment at a technical inspection location is made through the ministry's automated system at https://techinspection.mpwt.gov.kh, where the applicant creates an account and completes the required fields including personal information, a copy of the vehicle's import tax paper, and the identity card or residence book or family book of the vehicle owner. After completing the information the applicant prints the invoice and pays at a Wing or Ly Hour counter or from a personal account at selected banks.
